'''Marta Estrada Miyares''' (born 1946) is a [[Catalonia|Catalan]] researcher, with a career in [[oceanography]] and [[marine biology]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=November 2016 |editor-last=Catalan Society of Biology |title="La SCB celebra, el 9 de novembre, l'assemblea de socis i la sessió inaugural del curs 2016-2017" |url=https://ca.wikipedia.org/wiki/Societat_Catalana_de_Biologia }}</ref>{{Circular reference|date=September 2023}} Her most prominent studies are based on the [[Physiology|physiological]] characterization and [[Ecology|ecological]] impact of [[algae]] and [[phytoplankton]].<ref name=":5" />

== Career ==
Marta Estrada's parents were both amateur [[Archaeology|archaeologists]]. She was born in [[Granollers]], where she started her studies in the town's public elementary school. She later moved to [[Barcelona]], where she followed her education in Institut Verdaguer. She graduated with Honours and a brilliant academic record both in Biological Sciences (1968) and Medicine and Surgery (1970) at the [[University of Barcelona]]. At the end of her bachelor's studies, in 1969, she was awarded with the Prize for the most outstanding graduate of her BSc degree, the National Graduation Award and the Llaç de l'[[:ca:Orde Civil d'Alfons X el Savi|Orde Civil d'Alfons X el Savi]], a Spanish award for excellence in the education, science and research fields. Prior to that, in 1968, she received a scholarship to develop a doctoral thesis under the supervision of [[Ramon Margalef|Ramon Margalef López]]<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last1=Estrada |first1=Marta |last2=Alcaraz |first2=Miquel |date=2020-12-11 |access-date=2023-04-04 |title=The publications of Ramon Margalef in Investigación Pesquera and Scientia Marina: The beginnings of marine ecology in the CSIC |url=https://scientiamarina.revistas.csic.es/index.php/scientiamarina/article/view/1884 |journal=Scientia Marina |language=en |volume=84 |issue=4 |pages=445–461 |doi=10.3989/scimar.05107.30A |s2cid=229397396 |issn=1886-8134|doi-access=free |hdl=10261/225435 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> and the Institute of Fishery Research (IIP),<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Guerra Sierra |first=Ángel |title=El instituto de investigaciones pesqueras : tres décadas de historia de la investigación marina española |date=2003 |publisher=Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas |isbn=9788400081959 |location=Madrid |oclc=847423838}}</ref> that she defended in 1976 under the title ''Studies of populations of aquatic organisms in a non uniform medium''. As a result, she graduated as Doctor in [[Biology]] with a Prize for the most outstanding doctoral thesis from the [[University of Barcelona]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |title=Institut Memòria d'Estudis Catalans 2002-2003 |year=2004 |location=Barcelona |pages=189–190}}</ref>

In parallel, at the end of the 60s, Estrada was part of the scientific team of the research vessel ''Cornide de Saavedra'', which featured strongly in Spanish oceanographic research. Her roles included the control of the on-board [[computer]], the characterization of [[chlorophyll]] and [[primary production]], and recording [[temperature]], [[salinity]] and [[nutrient]] data. In 1971, she obtained the position of Scientific Collaborator at the IIP (currently Institute of Marine Sciences, ICM-CSIC), which she took in 1972 after a six-month stay at the [[Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution]] and on board of the [[Costa Rica|costa-rican]] research vessel ''Thompson''.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":2" /> This research stay in the [[United States|US]] allowed her to expand her doctoral thesis research thanks to a scholarship provided by the [[Institute of International Education]]  .

In the mid 70s, Marta Estrada started her specialization in the ecology of [[phytoplankton]] and populations of harmful [[algae]], from which she investigated mechanisms to control their [[Algal bloom|bloom]] events.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" /> She participated in two outstanding oceanic programs from the US, the ''Coastal Upwelling Ecosystems Analysis'' (CUEA) and the ''Organization of'' ''Persistent Upwelling Structures'' (OPUS), and performed expeditions in [[Peru|Perú]], [[Costa Rica]], north-eastern Africa and [[California]] as a collaboration between researchers of the IIP and the [[University of Washington]].<ref name=":5" /> During this time, she did extensive studies on phytoplankton's productivity and [[Biomass (ecology)|biomass]], [[nitrate]] consumption and natural composition.<ref name=":5" />

Later on, she advanced her research on phytoplankton and its interaction with the global marine ecosystem. She took part in multiple oceanographic expeditions in the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic, Arctic and Antarctic oceans. In 1984, she shared an expedition in the Antarctic Ocean with [[Josefina Castellví|Josefina Castellví Piulachs]] on board the Argentinian ''Almirante Irizar'', directed by Antoni Ballester Nolla.<ref name=":0" /> During this expedition, Marta Estrada and Josefina Castellví became the first Spanish to set foot on [[Antarctica]]. In the 80s, Estrada was designated chief of the department of Marine Biology and Oceanography at the Institute of Marine Sciences (ICM-CSIC), becoming the institute's director from 1995 to 1997.<ref name=":5" />

Marta Estrada has published numerous works in specialised international journals, books and chapters in volumes about [[Oceanography]].<ref name=":5" /> She has also participated in multiple international conferences and meetings, directed several PhD students and supervised many postdoctoral researchers. She has also taught lectures at the [[University of Barcelona]], the [[University of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria]] and the [[Menéndez Pelayo International University]].<ref name=":5" />

== Awards ==
Together with the academic distinctions received as a BSc and PhD, Estrada received the Trégouboff Award from the Parisian Academy of Sciences.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":3" /> In 1995, the [[Generalitat de Catalunya]] awarded her with the Medalla Narcís Monturiol for the scientific and technological merits,<ref name=":5" /> and in 2004, she was awarded with the [[Creu de Sant Jordi]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Marta Estrada i Miyares {{!}} enciclopèdia.cat |url=https://www.enciclopedia.cat/ec-gec-0522299.xml |access-date=2021-03-08 |website=www.enciclopedia.cat}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Creus de Sant Jordi 2004 |url=http://www.gencat.cat/presidencia/creusantjordi/2004/persones.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203132338/http://www.gencat.cat/presidencia/creusantjordi/2004/persones.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 3, 2013 }}</ref> In 2017, the Barcelona city council awarded her with the Honours Medal, together with the lawyer and politician [[Magda Oranich i Solagran|Magda Oranich]] and the singer José María Sanz Beltrán, Loquillo.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-07-21|title=Barcelona otorga su medalla de Honor a Loquillo, Oranich y Marta Estrada|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/local/barcelona/20170721/424281236444/barcelona-medalla-honor-loquillo-oranich-marta-estrada.html|access-date=2021-03-08|website=La Vanguardia|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Barcelona aprova les Medalles d'Honor del 2017 : Servei de Premsa|url=https://ajuntament.barcelona.cat/premsa/2017/07/21/barcelona-aprova-les-medalles-dhonor-del-2017/|access-date=2021-03-08|website=ajuntament.barcelona.cat}}</ref>

== Honours and institutional affiliations ==
Since 1996, she has been a member of the Catalan Society of Biology, becoming vicepresident<ref name=":3" /> and being distinguished as honorary member of the society in November 2016.<ref name=":0" /> She also became numerary member of the Biological Sciences Section of the Institute of Catalan Studies in 2011, giving a speech entitled ''Ecology of red tides''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Estrada Miyares |first=Marta |title=Ecologia de les marees roges: discurs de recepció de Marta Estrada i Miyares com a membre numerària de la Secció de Ciències Biològiques |date=2011 |publisher=Institut d'Estudis Catalans, Secció de Ciències Biològiques |isbn=978-84-9965-067-8 |edition=1st |location=Barcelona |oclc=796363910}}</ref> In December 1999 she was also named elected Academic of the Royal Academy of Arts and Sciences of Barcelona.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-08 |title=ESTRADA i MIYARES, Marta - Reial Acadèmia de Ciències i Arts de Barcelona |url=https://www.racab.cat/academics/numeraris/e/estrada |access-date=2023-04-04 }}</ref> In the entry celebration she gave a speech titled 'Hydrodynamics and phytoplankton of the Catalan sea'.

In 2016, the Granollers' High School was named after her, receiving the name IES Marta Estrada as a recognition of her scientific and technological merits.<ref>{{Cite web |last=NacióGranollers |date=2019-03-16 |title=L'Institut de Granollers passarà a dir-se Marta Estrada {{!}} NacióGranollers |url=https://www.naciodigital.cat/naciogranollers/noticia/25057/institut/granollers/passara/dir-se/marta/estrada |access-date=2023-04-04 }}</ref>

Other associations and entities of which Marta Estrada is or has been a member and/or affiliated to include:<ref name=":5" />

* ''ICES Advisory Committee on Marine Pollution'' (1989–1992)
* ''AD- ENA-WWF [[World Wide Fund for Nature|World Wildlife Foundation]]'' (1990–1992)
* ''Physiological Ecology of Harmful Algal Blooms'' (1992–1998)
* ''Scientific and Steering Committee'' (1998–2000) del programa internacional ''Global Ecology and Oceanography of Harmful Algal Blooms'' (GEOHAB) de la [[UNESCO]] (SCOR/IOC-UNESCO)
* ''Working Group 97'' del ''Special Committee on Oceanic Research'' (SCOR) del ''[[International Council for Science]]'' (ICSU)
* Several teams of experts about [[climate change]] in [[Catalonia]]
* Jury of the [[Ramon Margalef Prize in Ecology]]
* Centre Excursionista de Catalunya
